prompt:
A full slow-burn contemporary R&B song, about 3 minutes, with a real lead vocal. Male vocal, smooth and a little worn, soulful, intimate — like a late-night confession, with layered harmony stacks on the chorus. Warm Rhodes electric piano, deep round sub bass, crisp finger-snap percussion and soft brushed drums, subtle vinyl crackle under everything, a muted trumpet answering the vocal in the gaps. Tempo around 72 bpm, minor key, builds from sparse verse to full lush chorus, strips back to almost nothing on the bridge, then the last chorus comes in biggest with the harmonies wide. Ends on a soft Rhodes chord. Sung, not rapped. Here are the lyrics:

[Verse 1]
Two in the morning and the fryer's still on
Everybody clocked out, I'm the last one gone
Red neon in the window painting light on my hands
Nobody asked me, so nobody understands

[Pre-Chorus]
But I been building something quiet
While the whole block sleeps
Every hour that I'm burning
Is a promise that I keep

[Chorus]
I'm still here
Still standing in the smoke and the steam
I'm still here
And the floor don't fall out under me
You can check it, you can read it, every line
Ain't a secret in this kitchen of mine
I'm still here, oh, I'm still here

[Verse 2]
They said get a real job, said let the dream go
Said a boy with an apron got nothing to show
So I wrote it all down where anybody can see
No promises, baby, just receipts and me

[Pre-Chorus]
And I ain't asking for your pocket
I ain't selling you a line
I just kept the light on burning
When it was easy to let it die

[Chorus]
I'm still here
Still standing in the smoke and the steam
I'm still here
And the floor don't fall out under me
You can check it, you can read it, every line
Ain't a secret in this kitchen of mine
I'm still here, oh, I'm still here

[Bridge]
Low, low, keep it low
Let 'em talk and let 'em go
I ain't running, I ain't hiding
I'm just here until they know
Low, low, keep it low
Watch it grow, watch it grow

[Chorus]
I'm still here
Still standing in the smoke and the steam
I'm still here
And the floor don't fall out under me
Every hour, every shift, every night
I was here when the kitchen wasn't bright
I'm still here, oh, I'm still here
